title: From Technological Solutions to Health Data Governance in the Context of Personal Data Spaces: Citizen Panel Study
content: Background/Objectives: Personal Data Spaces (PDSs) are increasingly promoted as infrastructures for transparent and participatory health data governance. However, it remains unclear how citizens envision such governance in practice and which conditions they consider important for its implementation. This study explores citizens’ perspectives on health data governance in the context of PDSs, focusing on perceived feasibility, appropriateness, meaningfulness, and effectiveness. Methods: Two citizen panel sessions were conducted with 20 adults in Flanders, Belgium. Participants reflected on a desirable future of health data governance using a PDS-based scenario and identified conditions for its realization. Discussions were audio-recorded, transcribed, and thematically analyzed. Findings were subsequently organized using the FAME framework (feasibility, appropriateness, meaningfulness, and effectiveness). Results: Participants identified several governance-related conditions they considered important for realizing a desirable future of health data governance. Feasibility was associated with trusted and independent oversight, inclusive access, and integration with existing systems. Appropriateness was linked to context-sensitive data use and interpretation, with concerns about normative applications, political influence, and post-mortem data governance. Meaningfulness involved receiving tangible and personalized benefits, achieving manageable control and transparency, and recognizing that relying solely on individual choice may limit broader societal value, while emphasizing citizen involvement in defining collective benefits. Regarding effectiveness, participants identified potential value in using underutilized health data for prevention and early disease detection from a longitudinal perspective. Conclusions: Participants identified several governance conditions they considered important for realizing a desirable future of health data governance in the context of PDS. These findings suggest that implementing PDS may benefit from moving beyond technological solutions toward participatory governance models that combine trusted oversight, inclusive access, and meaningful citizen engagement.
